chain.label: Dark night over open water with essentially no outside visual references
chain.trigger: Evening civil twilight ended about 22 minutes before the accident; only 8 percent of the moon disk was illuminated and a scattered to broken stratiform layer overlay the Gulf

chain.label: Low-altitude flight beyond radar coverage with only 15-minute position reports, so no external check on altitude
chain.trigger: No radar returns were received after 1900:21 because the helicopter was no longer within the range of radar coverage; position reports every 15 minutes provided no continuous flight tracking

chain.label: SPZ-7000 DDAFCS gives no compelling annunciation of flight director source, coupling status, or unselected-axis command cue
chain.trigger: There is no aural or visual annunciation of a pilot-induced decouple... In general, the indications of either a pilot-induced or self-induced FD decouple were not particularly compelling

chain.label: Helicopter not equipped with TAWS and not required by regulation to be
chain.trigger: The accident helicopter was not equipped with a TAWS and was not required by Federal regulations to so be equipped

chain.label: Helicopter entered and remained in a shallow inadvertent descent from 1,800 feet toward the water
chain.trigger: The helicopter remained at 1,800 feet msl until about 1858:10 and then started to descend at a rate of about 300 feet per minute

caused_by.evidence: the pilots could have incorrectly programmed the flight director mode selector and either not have detected this situation or have misinterpreted it given the available system feedback

chain.label: Newly paired crew handling an in-flight destination change and its added workload minutes before impact
chain.trigger: The accident occurred about 4 minutes after the flight crew notified the dispatcher of the change in destination... The accident flight was the first one that paired the captain and the copilot

chain.label: Flight crew failed to monitor altitude and did not identify or arrest the descent, missing numerous cockpit cues
chain.trigger: the flight crew was not adequately monitoring the helicopter's altitude and missed numerous cues to indicate that the helicopter was inadvertently descending toward the water

caused_by.evidence: few, if any, references outside of the helicopter would have been available to the flight crew

a commercial flight-tracking system could have provided the Era Aviation dispatcher with information about the accident helicopter's descending altitude, which she could have communicated to the flight crew

if a TAWS had been installed aboard the accident helicopter, the system's aural and visual warnings should have provided the flight crew with ample time to recognize that the helicopter was descending toward the water
a change in destination increases pilot workload... new crew pairings have been associated with increased errors and less effective communication patterns

chain.label: Controlled flight into the Gulf of Mexico at high airspeed, shallow descent angle, near-level roll
chain.trigger: the helicopter crashed into the water at a high airspeed, a shallow descent angle, and a near-level roll attitude

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's failure to identify and arrest the helicopter's descent for undetermined reasons, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain
the flight crew's failure to identify and arrest the helicopter's descent... resulted in controlled flight into terrain

chain.label: Captain, copilot, and eight passengers killed by impact forces
chain.trigger: the cause of death for the flight crew and passengers was multiple blunt force trauma injuries

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable for the helicopter occupants because they were subjected to impact forces that exceeded the limits of human tolerance
